# Base-case results -- ciNPWT after instrumented posterior lumbar fusion

> **VERIFIED RESULTS -- Phase A2 full-text verification completed 2026-08-17: 46 of 48 parameters were closed out against the 14 source full texts and 43 carry a table/page locator; 2 remain unresolvable assumptions (the ciNPWT institutional net acquisition price and the superficial tunnel length). SSI/ciNPWT risk-threshold Markov CUA; US commercial payer; 2025 USD; monthly cycles; 24-cycle base horizon; 3%/yr discounting; WTP $100000/QALY.**

*Generated by `run_basecase.py` from the read-only engine (`inputs.py` / `model.py`). Model-based result; not a substitute for clinical evidence.*

## Model at a glance

- **Arms.** `A_standard` = Contemporary prevention + standard dressing; `B_cinpwt` = Contemporary prevention + ciNPWT. Universal *S. aureus* decolonization is background in **both** arms and cancels from every base-case increment.
- **Structure.** 5 clinical states expanded to an 18-slot engine vector (superficial tunnel 3 cycles, deep tunnel 12 cycles); monthly cycles; death absorbing.
- **Cohort.** Age 60, 53% male (both sourced to Urquhart 2021 [21] at A2); background mortality from the 2023 US life table; perioperative mortality 0.1% in cycle 0 only, identically in both arms.
- **Time and money.** Base horizon 24 cycles (2 years); scenarios 3, 12, 60 cycles. 3%/yr discounting on costs and QALYs; trapezoidal half-cycle correction on **dwell** streams only (tolls are point events, attributed whole). 2025 USD; WTP $100,000/QALY primary ($50,000 and $150,000 also reported).
- **Effect.** RR = 0.61 (0.49-0.76), applied to the onset hazard **inside the engine** (`p_ciNPWT = p_control x RR`), so the arms are correlated by construction and arm ordering holds in every draw.
- **Device.** ciNPWT $250 (`derived_assumption`; the single largest evidence gap, and the reason it is swept as an axis rather than fixed), charged once at cycle 0 in arm B. Standard-dressing differential $0 in the base case, charged at cycle 0 in arm A.

**There is no index-surgery cost and no well-state cost, by design.** The model is purely incremental: the index fusion, implant, ward stay and routine follow-up are identical in both arms and cancel exactly. Every "cost" below is therefore *incremental-versus-no-SSI* cost, **not** total cost of care, and must not be read as one.

Weighted 24-month incremental cost per SSI = **$44,784** (2025 USD; $53,680 deep / $18,795 superficial at a deep fraction of 0.745). Implied QALY loss per SSI = **0.0796**, i.e. $7,960 at $100,000/QALY. Those two numbers are the whole threshold arithmetic.

## Which SSI cost tranches are charged at each horizon

SSI cost enters as **three marginal Edmiston tranches** charged relative to the cycle of onset (`0`, `+6`, `+12` cycles). Onset is confined to the first 90 days, so entrants occupy `SUP_0`/`DEEP_0` at cycles 1-3; the three tranches therefore land at cycles 1-3, 7-9 and 13-15. **A toll falling beyond the horizon is not charged.** This is by design (BUILD-CONTRACT section 6.2), not a truncation error:

| Horizon | Cycles | Tranche 1 (onset, cycles 1-3) | Tranche 2 (onset+6, cycles 7-9) | Tranche 3 (onset+12, cycles 13-15) | Cost per SSI charged (2025 USD) |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---:|
| 90 d | 3 | **charged** | not charged | not charged | $28,534 |
| 1 y | 12 | **charged** | **charged** | not charged | $35,876 |
| 2 y (base case) | 24 | **charged** | **charged** | **charged** | $44,784 |
| 5 y | 60 | **charged** | **charged** | **charged** | $44,784 |

**The 1-year row is the trap.** Tranche 2 lands at cycles 7-9, comfortably *inside* a 12-cycle horizon, and is charged. Dropping it would silently remove $15,109 (deep) / $6,137 (superficial) in 2019 USD from every 1-year scenario, and the loss would look like a plausible horizon effect rather than a bug. Only the **90-day** horizon loses tranches 2 and 3 -- which is why the 90-day incremental cost is small and ciNPWT looks least attractive there. Note also that tranche 3 is charged whole at onset+12 but represents spending through months **25-27** post-index, so cost accrual reaches slightly past the nominal 2-year horizon; this is by design and is disclosed rather than truncated.

|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| low | 2.0% | `A_standard` | $882 | 1.3430 | 1.978 | 0.0199 |
| low | 2.0% | `B_cinpwt` | $788 | 1.3436 | 1.978 | 0.0122 |

| high | 11.4% | `B_cinpwt` | $3,318 | 1.3392 | 1.978 | 0.0693 |

| Risk stratum | Incremental cost | Incremental QALY | ICER | INMB @ $100,000 | CE quadrant | Dominance | NNT | SSIs prevented / 1,000 | Reoperations prevented / 1,000 |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| low | -$94 | +0.00061 | n/a (dominant) | $155 | NW | ciNPWT dominant | 128.6 | 7.8 | 2.2 |
| intermediate | -$886 | +0.00200 | n/a (dominant) | $1,086 | NW | ciNPWT dominant | 39.0 | 25.7 | 7.3 |
| high | -$1,712 | +0.00346 | n/a (dominant) | $2,057 | NW | ciNPWT dominant | 22.6 | 44.3 | 12.7 |

Incrementals are **`B_cinpwt` minus `A_standard`**. A negative incremental cost means ciNPWT *saves* money; with a positive incremental QALY that is **dominance** (CE quadrant `NW`), and the ICER is reported as `n/a` because a ratio is uninformative under strict dominance.

## Reading the strata

**Low risk (p = 2.0%, the Freire-Archer pooled deep SSI, rescaled to all-SSI [17] anchor).** Standard care accrues $882 of SSI-attributable cost per patient over two years and 19.9 SSIs per 1,000. ciNPWT prevents 7.8 SSIs per 1,000 (NNT 129) and 2.2 reoperations per 1,000, gains +0.00061 QALYs, and **saves $94** per patient -- INMB $155 at $100,000/QALY (**ciNPWT dominant**).

**Intermediate risk (p = 6.6%, the Edmiston all-SSI [12] anchor).** Standard care accrues $2,912 of SSI-attributable cost per patient over two years and 65.8 SSIs per 1,000. ciNPWT prevents 25.7 SSIs per 1,000 (NNT 39) and 7.3 reoperations per 1,000, gains +0.00200 QALYs, and **saves $886** per patient -- INMB $1,086 at $100,000/QALY (**ciNPWT dominant**).

**High risk (p = 11.4%, the Mueller 2021 control (14/123, instrumented, 60 d) [6] anchor).** Standard care accrues $5,030 of SSI-attributable cost per patient over two years and 113.7 SSIs per 1,000. ciNPWT prevents 44.3 SSIs per 1,000 (NNT 23) and 12.7 reoperations per 1,000, gains +0.00346 QALYs, and **saves $1,712** per patient -- INMB $2,057 at $100,000/QALY (**ciNPWT dominant**).

## Accrual / data-coverage disclosure

Share of the base-horizon **discounted** total accruing strictly after cycle 6 (6 months). The pivotal SSI hazard needs **no extrapolation** -- it is zero from day 91 -- but Edmiston's payment windows carry cost out to 24 months, so the post-6-month cost share is a real disclosure while the post-6-month QALY share simply reflects continued survival of the cohort.

**Two different shares are reported below and they are not interchangeable.** The plan's Decision 7 asks for the share of ***incremental*** cost and QALY accruing after 6 months -- that is **Table B**. Table A is the per-arm share of each arm's own total, which is descriptive only. The two differ substantially on the cost side: the ciNPWT device toll falls whole at cycle 0 and cancels much of the *early* SSI saving, so a larger fraction of the **net** increment accrues after 6 months than of either arm's own total -- most visibly at low risk, where the early saving is smallest. Reading the per-arm share as if it answered Decision 7 would understate how much of the decision-relevant cost lands late.

**Table A -- per arm** (share of that arm's own discounted total):

| Stratum | Arm | Discounted cost | Discounted QALYs | Cost after 6 mo (per arm) | QALYs after 6 mo (per arm) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| low | `A_standard` | $882 | 1.3430 | 35.8% | 72.2% |
| low | `B_cinpwt` | $788 | 1.3436 | 24.4% | 72.1% |
| intermediate | `A_standard` | $2,912 | 1.3394 | 35.8% | 72.2% |
| intermediate | `B_cinpwt` | $2,026 | 1.3414 | 31.3% | 72.2% |
| high | `A_standard` | $5,030 | 1.3357 | 35.8% | 72.3% |
| high | `B_cinpwt` | $3,318 | 1.3392 | 33.1% | 72.2% |

**Table B -- incremental (`B_cinpwt` minus `A_standard`) -- the plan's Decision 7 disclosure:**

| Stratum | Incremental cost | Incremental QALY | Incremental cost after 6 mo | Incremental QALYs after 6 mo |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| low | -$94 | +0.00061 | 130.7% | 50.8% |
| intermediate | -$886 | +0.00200 | 45.9% | 50.8% |
| high | -$1,712 | +0.00346 | 41.0% | 50.8% |

Both tables come from `accrual.csv`, which carries all four columns (`share_cost_after_6mo`, `share_qaly_after_6mo`, `share_inc_cost_after_6mo`, `share_inc_qaly_after_6mo`). The incremental shares are a property of the **stratum cell**, not of an arm, so `accrual.csv` repeats them identically on both arm rows -- filter to one arm before reading them and never sum them across arms. Where the incremental total is numerically zero the share is written as `NaN` and printed as `n/a` here: a share of a vanishing denominator is meaningless, so it is declared rather than reported as a large number.

## Cumulative expected events per 1,000 patients (2 y (base case))

Reoperations and persistent infections are **counters** (plan Decision 3): Edmiston's incremental payment is an all-cause spend that already contains readmission, I&D, revision and antibiotics, so these events carry **no** incremental cost anywhere in the engine. They exist to translate the result into clinical units and to feed the validation checks.

| Stratum | Arm | SSIs | Superficial | Deep | Reoperations | Persistent infections |

| low | `A_standard` | 19.9 | 5.1 | 14.9 | 5.7 | 3.7 |

## What these numbers do and do not carry

- **Verified.** Phase A2 full-text verification completed 2026-08-17: 46 of 48 parameters are closed out against the 14 source full texts and 43 carry a table/page locator. Only 2 still carry `verify=True` -- the ciNPWT institutional net acquisition price and the superficial tunnel length -- because no available source resolves either.
- **Cost is incremental-versus-no-SSI**, not total cost of care. Do not compare it with a published cost-per-fusion figure.
- **The absolute well-state utility (0.70) is an explicitly labelled assumption.** It is identical in both arms and enters the incremental QALY only through the small fraction of cohort-time that differs, so it scales each arm's QALY *level* but very nearly cancels from the *difference*.
- **Conservative-bias register** (all five bias against ciNPWT): no SSI-attributable mortality difference is assumed; the weaker all-surgery RR 0.61 is used rather than the favourable spine-specific RR 0.434; superficial-to-deep progression is omitted; the standard-dressing differential is set to $0 so arm B pays the full device cost with no offset; and the base case charges Pennington's matched attributable cost (m_ssi_cost = 0.492) rather than Edmiston's larger all-cause increment. One anti-conservative item is disclosed: `du_sup` is McFarland's *any-SSI* decrement applied to superficial SSI, and A2 upheld that objection rather than retiring it -- the only superficial-specific estimate in McFarland is a single null study at -0.03.
- **Competing mortality.** The cumulative 90-day onset *risk* reproduces the axis value `p` exactly, but the expected *count* of SSIs in the cohort sits ~0.3% below it because perioperative (cycle 0) and background mortality remove people from the at-risk pool. That is correct competing-risks behaviour, not a rounding error.
